Write flextable objects to one or multiple file formats

Source: R/ftwrite.R, R/writeFlextab.R
ftwrite.Rd

Writes flextable objects to various file formats with optional stamping (caption with script name, timestamp, and model information). Can write single flextables or lists of flextables, with automatic file naming and directory structure organization.

Usage

ftwrite(
  ft,
  file,
  formats,
  save = TRUE,
  show = !save,
  quiet = FALSE,
  script,
  time,
  model,
  stamp.ft.style,
  path.format = NULL,
  subdir = NULL,
  use.names = TRUE,
  stamp.format = NULL,
  stamp.funs = NULL,
  fun.path = NULL
)

writeFlextab(ft, file, script, formats, save, quiet = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

ft

A flextable object or a named list of flextable objects. If a list is provided, each element will be written to a separate file with names derived from the list element names.

file

Character string specifying the base file name to save to (without extension). The actual extension(s) will be determined by the formats argument. If ft is a list and elements are named, those names will be appended to this base file name.

formats

Character vector specifying one or more output formats. Supported formats are: "png", "docx", "pptx", "html", "rds". Default is NULL, which will infer the format from the file extension.

save

Logical. Should the table be saved to file? Default is TRUE. Set to FALSE to only return/show the flextable without saving. Hint: if you use a flag variable (like exportFlag), you can use save = exportFlag to control output generation.

show

Logical. Should the flextable be printed/displayed? Default is the opposite of save (i.e., !save). Combining save = TRUE and show = TRUE in knitr documents can be useful to display the table in the rendered document while also saving high-quality files.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses messages about files being written. Default is FALSE.

script

Character string or path to the script file. If provided, will be included in the table stamp/caption. This helps document which script generated the output.

time

Character string or POSIXct timestamp. The default behavior is to include a timestamp if script is provided. You can pass any string as time for a custom format, or use time = "" to omit the timestamp entirely.

model

Character string or model object specifying the model name/identifier. Used for stamping and for organizing output directories via path.format.

stamp.ft.style

A list of formatting options for the stamp, passed to ftstamp. Valid elements: size, align, space, bg, color.

path.format

Character string or function defining the output path. A template using %model, %script, and %name placeholders, or a function as returned by pathFormat. Passed to pathFormat. Default (NULL) uses file as is.

subdir

Character string specifying a subdirectory within the path structure. Used in conjunction with path.format.

use.names

Logical. If length(ft) > 1, should names(ft) be used in the output file names? Default is TRUE. If FALSE, numeric indices (1, 2, 3, ...) are used instead. Only used if save = TRUE and ft is a list.

stamp.format

A template for the stamp text using the placeholders %script, %time, %model, and %file, with "\n" for line breaks. Default is "%file\n%script\n%model\n%time". See createStamp.

stamp.funs

Optional named list of functions (elements script, time, model, file) used to preprocess the values before they are inserted into stamp.format. See createStamp.

fun.path

Deprecated. Use path.format.

...

Additional arguments passed to ftstamp for stamp customization.

Value

Invisibly returns the result from ftwriteOne (for lists, returns results for all written tables). If show = TRUE, also prints the flextable(s) to the current device.

Details

The function handles both single flextable objects and lists of flextables:

  • For single flextables: writes to file(s) with name specified by file

  • For lists of flextables: writes each element to a separate file, with names constructed from file and the list element names

When ft is a list:

  • Named list elements use their names in the output file names

  • Unnamed elements are automatically numbered with zero-padded indices

Multiple formats can be written simultaneously by specifying a vector of formats. Each format will be saved as a separate file with the appropriate extension.

Functions

  • writeFlextab(): Deprecated function name. Use ftwrite.

File Formats

The following formats are supported via the flextable package save functions:

  • "png": Image format via save_as_image

  • "docx": Microsoft Word via save_as_docx

  • "pptx": Microsoft PowerPoint via save_as_pptx

  • "html": HTML format via save_as_html

  • "rds": R data format (saves the flextable object itself)

See also

ftwriteOne for writing a single flextable, ftstamp for adding stamps to flextables, writer for a unified interface to write various object types, pathFormat for organizing output directories, save_as_image, save_as_docx, save_as_pptx, save_as_html

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(flextable)

# Create a simple flextable
ft1 <- flextable(head(mtcars))

# Write to PNG (default format)
ftwrite(ft1, file = "mytable")

# Write to multiple formats
ftwrite(ft1, file = "mytable", formats = c("png", "docx", "html"))

# Write with stamping
ftwrite(ft1, file = "mytable",
        script = "analysis.R",
        model = "run001")

# Write a list of tables
ft_list <- list(
  summary = flextable(summary(mtcars)),
  head = flextable(head(mtcars)),
  tail = flextable(tail(mtcars))
)
ftwrite(ft_list, file = "tables", formats = "docx")
# Creates: tables_summary.docx, tables_head.docx, tables_tail.docx

# Use with path structure for model organization
ftwrite(ft1, file = "summary",
        model = "run001",
        path.format = "%model/%name_%model")
# Writes to: run001/summary_run001.png
} # }
